_comment: The single source of every pinned native version. Every other copy (Gradle, Package.swift, example app, CI) is asserted against this file by test/native_versions_test.dart.

flutter.provenance: Raised from 3.41.0 (the first release where a SwiftPM-only plugin resolves on Linux/Windows) to 3.50.0 / Dart 3.14.0 for the 10.0 major: Direct Interop (JNIgen and FFIgen for Objective-C stable, Pigeon interop mode in preview), AGP 9 and `material_ui` are only there from 3.50 (flutter.dev/blog/whats-new-in-flutter-3-50, 2026-11). Competitor floors (pub.dev, 2026-10-20): Sentry 3.44, Firebase/Datadog 3.27, Bugsnag/Shake/Embrace 3.10, Instabug 1.17.

android.provenance: Maven Central latest, 2026-11-17 (moved from 7.5.1; the plugin stays 4.1.1, the latest, tag v4.1.1). 7.6.0 changes behaviour, not the wrapper SPI: ReportingTriggerByShake and ReportingTriggerByNotification default to false, the HttpURLConnection response body arrives as a later event, the binary and JSON serializers and the logcat reader are hardened. Gradle plugin must be >= 4.0.7 (workbook 1.4). sdkBuild is the commit the SDK prints in its banner (`Bugsee Android SDK 7.6.0 [2a88ea7fbf]`: 10 characters, the tag v7.6.0 is 2a88ea7fb; read from a run on a physical phone, 2026-11-17): the device verification harness (scripts/device) matches it, because a version string alone cannot tell two builds of the same version apart (workbook 9.1.1).

jdk.provenance: The supported set is what CI runs (Zulu 21) and the SDK documents. Gradle 8.14 (the old Flutter template) could not parse JDK 25; the example on Gradle 9.3.1 built a debug APK with JDK 25 (measured 2026-11-17), which does not make 25 supported.

ios.provenance: Stable 7.1.0 (moved from 7.0.1 on 2026-11-17): tag 7.1.0 of bugsee/spm (465ec10) and bugsee/feedback-spm (879875e), SDK source `origin/release@b65bdca06` of bugsee/bugsee-cocoa (the iOS source repository has no 7.x tag). sdkBuild is what the SDK prints in its banner (`Bugsee IOS SDK ver:7.1.0 build:b65bdca06-9`: the commit and its count), read from the string in the 7.1.0 binary of the tag's xcframework (not yet from a run: the device verification harness, workbook 9.1.1, matches it on the next run). 7.1.0 over 7.0.1: the wrapper SPI headers are unchanged (only BugseeOptions.h comments differ: the shake trigger defaults to NO, span URL redaction is documented); the new SwiftPM product BugseeCrashExtension is for an app's Crash Reporter Extension target (iOS 27+) and the wrapper does not link it. Earlier builds: 7.0.1 `5c6b9d9db-8`, 7.0.0 `2b88480fa-7`, beta7 `9854b7e50-15`.

feedback.provenance: The optional in-app chat, a separate package (PLAN.md D4) mirroring the native split. Its Android artifact is published at the same version as android.sdk (Maven Central, 2026-11-12: bugsee-android-feedback 7.5.1, which depends on bugsee-android 7.5.1); its iOS product is BugseeFeedback of feedbackSpmUrl at ios.sdk (it pins bugsee/spm exactly to the same tag). The feedback package's Gradle and Package.swift repeat these pins as literals (a published copy has no native-versions.json next to it) and test/feedback_package_drift_test.dart compares them.

pigeon.provenance: pub.dev, published 2026-10-07 (latest at the time was 29.0.11, 2026-10-20); needs Dart ^3.11.0. Not a dependency of the plugin (it requires meta >=1.18; Flutter 3.41.0, the floor when this was decided, shipped 1.17.0, the 3.50.0 floor ships 1.19.0, so it could be a dev_dependency now and has not been moved): it runs from the pure-Dart package in pigeons/, locked by pigeons/pubspec.lock.

optionsManifest.provenance: Both SDKs publish an immutable options-manifest.json per release (bugsee/specs sdk/options, manifestVersion 1), generated from the live option registry: android/7.5.1.json (generatedAt 2026-11-11) and ios/7.0.1.json (generatedAt 2026-11-03), android fetched 2026-11-12, ios 2026-11-03, vendored verbatim as android.json / ios.json in fixtureDir. `dart scripts/sync_option_manifests.dart --check` (weekly, native-pins.yml) refetches and diffs; everything else reads the committed copies offline.
